group: block-list rewriting, coin-like block lengths (rule not found)
title: What is known about 1RB1RC_1RC1RB_1LD0RA_1LE1LD_1LF0LC_0LA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RC_1RC1RB_1LD0RA_1LE1LD_1LF0LC_0LA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open, and it is now the Pascal machine's question. This table is the table of 1RB0RE_0RC---_1LD1LE_1LE1LD_1RF0LC_1RA1RF in a mirror, started in state C: every bounce writes the next row of Pascal's triangle mod 2, an odd frozen block halts, and the machine never halts if that machine's list program never fails from EO [b, a, b, a] none 1 (all Lean, kernel). The list program ran 40,000 steps from there without failing.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: Where a halt can come from
claims.text: If the machine halts on its third step from a configuration, that configuration is one of: D with 1 two left, 0 left, 0 under the head. So a run can reach a halt only through one of these patterns, and a proof that the machine never halts only has to rule them out. The proof splits on the state and the five cells around the head.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 65,183 cells have been visited and 49,646 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.085). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.506).

claims.title: Blocks of length 4k + 3
claims.text: At each visit of the left end up to step 5.2·108, every block of 1s except the first two and the last has length 4k + 3; the counts for k = 0, 1, 2, … halve at each step (2,665, 1,336, 716, 315, … of 5,366 at step 522,867,988). Observed in simulation, not proved.

claims.title: Rounds grow by about 1.75
claims.text: Between consecutive long gaps the list, read as a word with 4k + 3 ↦ 1^k 0, grows from 26 to 97, 351, 1,136, 3,508, 10,746 letters every second round (about 1.75 a round), and the step count by about 3.1 a round.

claims.title: Regular-language deciders tried (F11)
claims.text: None of these closes: each reaches a halting configuration in its abstraction, which says nothing about whether the machine halts. n-gram CPS (tools/c/ngramcps.c), equal widths on both sides: a halting local configuration is reached with plain up to width 24, history 1 up to width 24, history 2 up to width 24, history 3 up to width 24, LRU history up to width 6 (larger widths ran out of the 150 s or 60 million configuration budget). n-gram CPS with every cell tagged by its position mod p: fails for p = 2 up to width 20, p = 3 up to width 20, p = 4 up to width 20, p = 6 up to width 20. n-gram CPS where each side also carries the state of a small automaton that has read that side from the far end (every automaton with up to 3 states on both sides, or 4 states on one side), with position mod 1..4 and widths 4, 6, 8: no closed set without a halt in all 120 parameter sets. Run-length windows (the K nearest runs of equal macro cells on each side, run lengths kept exactly below T and mod M above): fails for all 72 parameter sets (cells of 1 to 4 bits, K = 2, 4, 6, T = 2, 4, M = 1, 2, 4). Two-automaton closed tape language by SAT (a deterministic automaton reading each side inward, n states each, CaDiCaL): no solution for n = 2..7; n = 8 not finished in 150 s.
claims.where: sweeps of 13 November 2026 (family F11); the tagged and run-length deciders are not in the repository yet

claims.title: The Pascal machine in a mirror
claims.text: This table is the table of 1RB0RE_0RC---_1LD1LE_1LE1LD_1RF0LC_1RA1RF read in a mirror, with that machine's states A to F renamed E, F, A, B, C, D. The blank tape is its own mirror image, so the run from blank tape is, cell for cell in the mirror, the run of the Pascal table started in state C, and this machine halts if and only if that run halts.

claims.title: One bounce is one row of Pascal's triangle mod 2
claims.text: Every theorem of the Pascal machine's folder holds here with left and right exchanged; its Lean files are compiled here unchanged (lean/P75625/). At a left turn in C, with the zone right of the head a word in the 4-cell letters 0111 and 1111 and the frozen tape 1 1 1 ... left of it, one bounce turns the zone into the next row of Pascal's triangle mod 2 (closed form by Lucas' theorem), and takes two cells from the frozen block. A frozen block of odd length followed by 0 1 halts, whatever the zone, clean or walled (the halt: D reading 0 with 0 and then 1 to its left).

claims.title: The holdout is the Pascal machine's list program, from another start
claims.text: The first left turn in C, at step 26, is the list state EO [b, a, b, a] none 1 of the Pascal machine's list machine arun (zone b a b a). If that list machine never fails from there, this machine never halts. The Pascal machine's own run starts it at EO [b, a] none 1.

claims.title: Where the list machine can fail
claims.text: For every state: a turn with no lone 1 in the zone never fails; a crossing turn with a clean far part whose tape ends in a single 1 never fails, and plain and crossing turns ending in a single 1 hand that on. So the list machine fails only at a crossing turn with blank end, at an EO turn during a crossing, or at a crossing turn whose far part is not clean.

claims.title: The list machine from this start: 40,000 steps
claims.text: Run on its own, 40,000 list steps without a failure (zone up to 21,498 letters, every far part clean). None of the 19 EO turns comes during a crossing, so there is not a single crossing turn with blank end: the first way the list machine can fail never even comes up. In lockstep with the real machine the list machine agrees at all 17,728 right turns of the first 2·108 steps.
claims.where: py/mirror_run.py of the folder of 1RB1RA_1LC0RF_1LD1LC_1LE0LB_0LF---_1RA1RB (run C 40000, lockstep C 2e8)

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It halts exactly if the Pascal table started in C halts (Lean), and it never halts if the Pascal machine's list machine never fails from EO [b, a, b, a] none 1 (Lean). Whether it fails is the same open question as for the Pascal machine, from another start.

claims.text: The same table as 1RB1RA_1LC0RF_1LD1LC_1LE0LB_0LF---_1RA1RB up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0LE_1RC1RB_1RD0RA_0RE---_1LF1LA_1LA1LF up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. The machine keeps rewriting a long list of blocks of 1s whose lengths look like the results of coin flips, and each round makes the list about 1.75 times longer. What a round does to the list has not been worked out.

facts.text: The Pascal machine's table read in a mirror, started in state C.
Each bounce writes the next row of Pascal's triangle mod 2.
Steps of the list program from this start, without a failure.

sections.heading: A list of blocks
html: Each time the head reaches the left end, the tape is a list of blocks of 1s separated by single 0s. Except at the two ends, every block has length 4k + 3, and k behaves like the length of a run of heads in fair coin flips: half the blocks have k = 0, a quarter k = 1, and so on. At step 522,867,988 there are 5,366 blocks:

sections.heading: The Pascal machine, in a mirror
html: Read the table of 1RB0RE_0RC---_1LD1LE_1LE1LD_1RF0LC_1RA1RF in a mirror and rename its states A to F as E, F, A, B, C, D: you get this machine's table exactly. The blank tape looks the same in a mirror, so this machine's run is that machine's table started in state C, seen in a mirror. Lean checks the correspondence, and every theorem about that table comes over with left and right exchanged.

So the picture of that machine applies. A zone next to the growing right end is a word in the 4-cell letters 0111 and 1111. Each time the head turns left in C, one bounce sweeps the zone and replaces it by its running parity, the next row of Pascal's triangle mod 2: the nested triangles in the space-time diagram above. Each bounce takes two cells from the frozen block left of the head. A frozen block of odd length followed by 0 1 would halt the machine, whatever the zone.

After 26 steps the run is in a state of the Pascal machine's list program, which follows the machine from turn to turn using lists alone. Lean proves that if this program never fails from EO [b, a, b, a] none 1, the machine never halts. It ran 40,000 list steps from there without failing. Lean also proves the program can fail in only three ways.

sections.heading: Sweeps that rewrite the whole list
html: The head sweeps across the whole list again and again: a sweep to the right turns each block into a string of short runs, and the sweep back turns that into blocks again, changed. Between the long gaps when the head stays away from the left end, the list grows by about 1.75:
(letters: the list read as a word, block 4k + 3 standing for k ones and a zero). What a round does to that word is not known.

sections.heading: Not known
html: The machine stops only if the head in state F reads a 1; in 109 simulated steps that never happens. Without the round rule there is no honest estimate. The coin-like block lengths suggest a pseudo-random word being rewritten, as in the Collatz-like holdouts.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.085). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.506).
After 109 steps the tape spans 65,183 cells (190 left of the start, 43,143 right), with a density of 1s of 0.762.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB1RA_1LC0RF_1LD1LC_1LE0LB_0LF---_1RA1RB: rename A→F, B→A, C→B, D→C, E→D, F→E; it is this table started in state B
  • 1RB0LE_1RC1RB_1RD0RA_0RE---_1LF1LA_1LA1LF: rename A→E, B→F, C→A, D→B, E→C, F→D and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state C, in a mirror
  • 1RB0RE_0RC---_1LD1LE_1LE1LD_1RF0LC_1RA1RF: rename A→C, B→D, C→E, D→F, E→A, F→B and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state E, in a mirror

Same tapes at another pace (observed, not proved). Leave the states aside and compare only the tape and the place of the head. Then a large part of the first 107 configurations of this machine are configurations of the machines below, in the same order and up to the end of the run. The steps at which they occur differ, the tables are not renamings of each other, and equal tapes with different states may be continued differently, so this does not tie the halting questions together.

  • 1RB0RB_1LC---_0LA1LD_1RE0LC_1RF1RE_1RA0RD (in a mirror): 4,990,813 configurations, the last at step 6,660,591 here and step 10,000,000 there

summary: The Pascal machine (1RB0RE_0RC---_1LD1LE_1LE1LD_1RF0LC_1RA1RF) in a mirror, started in state C: bounces write rows of Pascal's triangle mod 2, and in Lean it halts only if that machine's list program fails from another start; open.
